Minors (Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 31-13, 31-14, 31-18, 31-23): rules encoded for mercantile (retail) establishments. Under-16 may not work in mercantile/restaurant at all (§ 31-23(a)) except 15-year-olds as bagger/cashier/stock clerk in school vacations of 5+ days, and on Saturdays in a retail food store; encoded as a 0 h weekly cap for 14 and a 0 h school-day cap for 15. Restaurants (§ 31-18) have the same 6 h/32 h/48 h limits with an 11 p.m./midnight night limit.

Minors: 16-17 school-day cap is 8 h when the school day precedes a non-school day (Friday); the validator applies 6 h on Friday (stricter). Supermarkets (>3,500 sq ft) may keep 16-17 until midnight before non-school days; encoded 11 p.m.

rules.summary: During school vacations (5+ days), 15-year-olds may work in a mercantile establishment as a bagger, cashier or stock clerk at most 8 hours a day and 40 a week, 7 a.m.-7 p.m. (9 p.m. July 1-Labor Day).

rules.summary: Students 16-17 in mercantile establishments may work at most 6 hours on a school day (8 before a non-school day and on other days) and 32 hours in a school week, 6 a.m.-10 p.m. (11 p.m., supermarkets midnight, before a non-school day).

citation.title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 31-13 — Hours of labor of minors in mercantile establishments
citation.excerpt: more than (1) six hours in any regularly scheduled school day unless the regularly scheduled school day immediately precedes a nonschool day or eight hours in any other day, and (2) thirty-two hours

rules.summary: When school is not in session, 16- and 17-year-olds in mercantile establishments may work at most 8 hours a day and 48 a week, 6 a.m.-11 p.m. on nights not before a school day (supermarkets midnight).

citation.title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 31-14 — Night work of minors regulated
citation.excerpt: No person under eighteen years of age shall be employed in any manufacturing, mechanical or mercantile establishment between the hours of ten o'clock in the evening and six o'clock in the morning
